title: Dillingham
setting: During the first big salmon run, a new worker learns the pace of a Bristol Bay cannery from the people beside him. The line, the separate dorms, and Sunday dinner in the mess hall give the crew three very different places to catch their breath.

cast.name: Beaver
cast.description: Teal chest and broad tail. Eager to take on his first big run, even when he needs help finding his rhythm.
cast.appearance: Teal chest, brown fur, broad tail, and the cannery’s hairnet and earplugs on the production floor.

cast.name: John
cast.description: Pigtails and black gloves. He knows how the line moves and makes time to show Beaver the ropes.
cast.appearance: Pigtails, black gloves, and production-floor safety gear.

cast.name: Bear
cast.description: Brown fur and a big thermos. He brings a calm presence to a shift that can turn busy in a moment.
cast.appearance: Brown fur and a large thermos.

reader_art: Beaver, John, and Bear on The First Big Run cast sheet
Cast sheet from Dillingham: The First Big Run

title: Riggins
setting: Riggins and the Meepmops share a clay-built world where the small details carry the story. A familiar morning routine makes room for company, and the closing pages linger on the pleasure of staying together one minute longer.

cast.name: Riggins
cast.description: The story introduces Riggins through an ordinary morning. Coffee and unhurried gestures set the pace.
cast.appearance: Long brown hair, human eyes, and a clay-built likeness.

cast.name: The Meepmops
cast.description: Their small scale changes how a room feels. Their company gives Riggins a reason to pause.
cast.appearance: Black clay, tan circular eyes and ring mouths. Two arms total, including the arm on the head.

reader_art: Art from Riggins: A Place for the Small Things

title: PenPals
setting: An unaddressed letter turns a desk into an adventure map. Drawers, scraps, and narrow spaces become places to explore, and the friends’ different ways of making marks shape how they solve problems.

cast.name: Yellow Pencil
cast.description: Sketches possibilities before all the details are settled.
cast.appearance: Yellow pencil body.

cast.name: Red Test Pencil
cast.description: Blunt and precise, with a tender side that comes out when someone needs room.
cast.appearance: Red test-pencil body.

cast.name: Blue Pencil
cast.description: Spots small traces others pass by.
cast.appearance: Blue colored-pencil body.

cast.name: Pen
cast.description: Gives wandering ideas a shape the group can work with.
cast.appearance: Pen-shaped stationery body.

cast.name: Crayon
cast.description: Brings big energy, jokes, and unexpected ways forward.
cast.appearance: Crayon-shaped stationery body.

cast.name: Stub
cast.description: Can reach places the other friends cannot fit into.
cast.appearance: Short pencil silhouette.

reader_art: Pencils, pen and crayon from the PenPals cast
Cast sheet from PenPals: The Letter That Wouldn’t Leave

title: Raiders
setting: The Long Way Home follows five friends in a hand-drawn Aurora, Colorado. Their senior year starts on a yellow school bus and grows into a story about who gets to make space for art, friendship, and a night of their own. Aurora bends into little-planet views that echo the images in Micah’s sketchbook.

cast.name: Micah Ryder
cast.description: The senior-year lead sketches curved versions of Aurora. In Margin Play, his hometown becomes an explorable action-RPG setting.
cast.appearance: Pale skin, angular black hair with electric-blue spikes, huge dark eyes, black clothes, and oversize hands and shoes.

cast.name: Dawna Avery
cast.description: Makes her own zines and helps organize the group’s art-and-music show.

cast.name: Venna Vale
cast.description: A photographer with an independent eye who wants her submissions to speak for themselves.
cast.appearance: Purple hair with straight bangs, rectangular glasses, medium-brown skin, black shirt and purple trousers.

cast.name: Gio Calder
cast.description: A musician who wants someone to hear his song.

cast.name: Jace Mercer
cast.description: Thinks big about what the friends can stage together.

links: Game · Raiders: Different Doors, Same Sky

plates.caption: Original Raiders cast and logo illustration

projects: Volume One script and original character artwork.
Party action RPG built around the Aurora cast, hands-on tactics, and the art-and-music show.

title: Deathwish Garden
setting: In The Hour That Would Not End, dawn stalls over a crooked cemetery town beneath the Zodiac Clock. Hope and Despair work at an afterlife help desk. When the clock takes Hope, Despair has to ask the Kingdom to help bring him home.

cast.name: Despair
cast.description: A haloed spirit with three head points, two arms, and a flowing tail. His visible heart carries the cost of taking on other people’s grief.
cast.appearance: In Deathwish, three head points, two arms, a halo, a spectral tail and a visible heart.

cast.name: Hope
cast.description: A spectral companion with two arms, a flowing tail, and a heart that shows what he feels.
cast.appearance: In Deathwish, two arms, a spectral tail and a visible heart.

cast.name: Nell
cast.description: A small skeleton clerk with a bob haircut who keeps the help desk running.
cast.appearance: Small skeleton with a bob haircut.

links: Read · Memorandum in a Cruet, the inspiration for The Cruet

plates.caption: DeathWish promotional art featuring the two spirits

projects: The Hour That Would Not End
A DeathWish story set around the Zodiac Clock.
A DeathWish graphic novel inspired by Memorandum in a Cruet.

title: Kingdom Kitty
setting: A paper-built adventure world of folding scenery, small feline heroes, and shadowy creatures. The same character designs have been explored in role-playing and puzzle formats.

cast.name: Sora Kitty
cast.description: One of the central trio. The hero’s design carries the story from the printed page to a 3D paper world.
cast.appearance: Round white kitty with whiskers and a distinctive hairstyle.

cast.name: Kairi Kitty
cast.description: Part of the central trio, with a dedicated model in the character roster.
cast.appearance: Round white kitty with whiskers and her own hairstyle.

cast.name: Riku Kitty
cast.description: The third lead, also modeled as a distinct paper-world character.
cast.appearance: Round white kitty with whiskers and his own hairstyle.

cast.name: Shadow kitties
cast.description: The enemy designs play against the softness of the paper environments.

title: Mister Mikey
setting: Mikeyland is an island drawn in ballpoint where paths and places can lose their connections. Mikey learns that a line holds when the inhabitants remember and maintain what it connects. Mister Mikey also has a separate crossover design in Collision Course.

cast.name: Mikey
cast.description: The Wander drawing gives him a round head, large oval eyes, red cap and shirt, and blue trousers.
cast.appearance: Round head, large oval eyes, red cap and shirt, and blue trousers.

cast.name: Angel
cast.description: A smiling, winged spirit with a halo who remembers people and the details of their lives.
cast.appearance: Smiling, winged spirit with a halo.

cast.name: Demon
cast.description: A dark spirit with a three-point head and a red broken heart. He spots weak edges on the island’s routes.
cast.appearance: Dark three-point silhouette and a red broken heart.

cast.name: Golden
cast.description: The retriever gives the journey personal stakes.
cast.appearance: Retriever with a damaged ear.

cast.name: Massive
cast.description: The armored figure works to hold the island together.
cast.appearance: Unfinished armor with square fragments.

cast.name: Mister Mikey in Collision Course
cast.description: A blond, sword-carrying figure with torn clothes, a missing arm, and black high-tops.
cast.appearance: Blond hair, missing arm, torn clothes, sword and black high-tops.

title: Punk Skeleton
setting: This character starts with the graphic contrast of a skull and a punk silhouette. The old sketchbook includes a punk skull study, and the 3D roster explores a skeleton with a mohawk.

cast.name: Punk Skeleton
cast.description: A mohawk breaks up the recognizable skull shape and gives the character its profile.
cast.appearance: Skull with a mohawk silhouette.

plates.caption: Punk Skeleton profile and back studies

title: Xero / Zero
setting: Xero began as a browser-playable GameMaker project. The later design expands into a looping neon city, with rooftop traversal, grind rails and grappling, plus off-world areas that turn gravity around the player.

cast.name: Xero
cast.description: A compact silver robot with a swept-back helmet, pale eye area and separate armor plates. The city comic follows a capable rescue worker with dry humor, jets, and a transforming hand cannon.
cast.appearance: Compact silver body, swept-back helmet, pale eye area, and separate plates.

title: AR3NA All-Stars
setting: AR3NA is an arcade sports and competition world. Its courts support ideas ranging from volleyball and foosball to snowballs and dodgeball, with slopes, ledges and other movement features connecting sports to platforming.

cast.name: Red / Yellow
cast.description: Alternating red and yellow spikes, with larger shapes at the crown and smaller shapes around the ears and neck, make this design recognizable from several angles.
cast.appearance: Alternating spikes, largest at the crown.

cast.name: Pink & Blue
cast.description: Blue eyes and bangs lead into pink hair.
cast.appearance: Blue eyes and bangs with pink hair.

cast.name: Stripes
cast.description: Blonde hair, a backwards baseball cap, and a green-blue striped top.
cast.appearance: Blonde hair, backwards baseball cap, and a green-blue striped top.

cast.name: Black Beanie
cast.description: A separate teammate distinguished by the headwear silhouette.
cast.appearance: Black beanie silhouette.

title: Klay Karts
setting: A clay-styled kart racer with nine circuits and a crossover grid. The world has its own handmade terrain and sense of scale. The kart seat, driving pose, and camera distance change how familiar characters read on the track.

cast.name: Crossover drivers
cast.description: Familiar faces from different worlds share the track. The seated variants keep their silhouettes recognizable while fitting inside each kart.
cast.appearance: Seated poses carry familiar silhouettes into the clay-styled karts.

title: Ex, Can & Spray
setting: The early portfolio includes a spray-can illustration. Ex, Can & Spray also appear as a group in Collision Course, where they help brace a route during the rescue. The artwork here is the original spray-can study.

cast.name: Ex, Can & Spray
cast.description: The trio brings its own visual language to the crossover, where they work as a group.

image: Spray-can study from the portfolio archive

title: Odonis Orphane 2
setting: The second Odonis Orphane book follows the trail from the snowy settlement of Rime toward the Glass Coast. A broken-halo mark on a freight crate connects the destinations. The graphic novel uses rough ink, open white space, and selective color.

cast.name: Odonis Orphane
cast.description: A lanky yellow alien with large turquoise eyes and asymmetrical white hair. He travels on a patched snowboard and uses movement to sustain the energy blade that forms from his hand.
cast.appearance: Lanky yellow alien with turquoise eyes, asymmetrical white hair, and a patched snowboard.

cast.name: Ilex
cast.description: A courier with short dark hair, crescent ears, and a satchel. She recognizes the freight mark that leads toward the coast.
cast.appearance: Short dark hair, crescent ears, and a courier satchel.

cast.name: Marn
cast.description: Mentors Odonis during his time in Rime.
cast.appearance: Rounded alien silhouette, apron, and head covering.

cast.name: Vale
cast.description: Helps repair the board and preserve Rime’s records.
cast.appearance: Long dark coat, cracked pale visor, and hooked staff.

links: Book · Odonis Orphane: The Unwritten Line

title: Hope and Despair
setting: Collision Course depicts the white-haired Hope and dark-haired Despair alongside their spectral counterparts from Deathwish. They have their own appearances and memories and can be present in the same scene.

cast.name: Hope
cast.description: White-haired humanoid counterpart with an identity and memories of his own.

cast.name: Despair
cast.description: Dark-haired humanoid counterpart who appears alongside the spirits in Collision Course.

plates.caption: Original Hope and Despair humanoid drawing
Early Hope and Despair illustrated pair

title: Mannequin Fighter
setting: Originally called Inquiry, this illustrated project also became the basis for a 3D fighter. Its mannequin forms make body language, pose and shape part of the visual identity.

cast.name: Heart model
cast.description: The central mannequin design in the project.

image: Mannequin Fighter: After Hours cover art
Public game artwork · Mannequin Fighter: After Hours

title: Splinter & Fuse
setting: Crumble’s demolition duo grew out of two axemen on a 2008 sketchbook page. The comic puts the pair in an argument over what gets torn down and what their neighbors get to keep.

cast.name: Splinter
cast.description: Sells the plan before thinking it through, then throws himself into making it happen.
cast.appearance: Yellow star-shaped bangs, blue hair at the back, pointed nose, white tee, blue shorts, and heavy sneakers.

cast.name: Fuse
cast.description: Spots the details everyone else missed and quietly proposes the more outrageous plan.
cast.appearance: Red jagged bangs and spikes, worried eyes, pointed nose, black tee with a white symbol, and gray shorts.

cast.name: Dot
cast.description: Practical, competitive, and quick with a reply.
cast.appearance: Purple twin buns, yellow jacket, black shorts, and purple sneakers.

cast.name: Rivet
cast.description: Built Bob and keeps track of what the duo breaks.
cast.appearance: Teal undercut, orange overalls, goggles and gloves.

cast.name: Bob
cast.description: A lent-out machine with a personality of its own.
cast.appearance: Yellow spherical body, a single round eye, and treads.

plates.caption: Original 2008 sketchbook reference · Splinter at upper left and Fuse at lower right

projects: The first issue follows the duo and a borrowed demolition robot through Crumble.

title: Mosswake
setting: A top-down survival and building world shaped by elevation, tides, and player construction. The map is designed to keep changing over time, so returning to a familiar spot can reveal a different shoreline or settlement.

cast.name: Survivor
cast.description: The player builds, explores, and adapts to a persistent landscape.

title: Avalanca
setting: A downhill world of snowy slopes, forest trails, and changing weather. Different courses and vehicles change where the player can carry speed, jump, or cut across terrain.

cast.name: Rider
cast.description: The player can ride a snowboard or skis, with bicycles, scooters and watercraft extending the downhill design to other surfaces.

title: Ortega Sauce
setting: Fashion shows and DJ sets share the same journey across venues. Runway and deck sequences use rhythm, while outfits, travel and rapport give the player ways to build a career between performances.

cast.name: Performer
cast.description: The playable role spans fashion and music. Clothes, hairstyles and accessories give the same performer different silhouettes for different venues.
cast.appearance: Outfits, hairstyles, and accessories change with the venue.

title: A Rocket’s Intensity
setting: A space arcade world that moves between orbit, wormholes, open space, and city flight. Each setting changes the pilot’s horizon and the room available for a maneuver.

cast.name: Pilot
cast.description: The ship is the playable focus, with barrel rolls and changes in viewpoint tying different flight settings together.

plates.caption: Original ship, craft, and celestial sprite studies
Early game artwork and UFO study

title: Collision Course
setting: The Space Between brings cast members from across the catalog to Interchange, a station caught between worlds. A damaged relay strands its travelers. Recovering the routes means learning how each world’s materials and rules behave at the station.

cast.name: Lina
cast.description: A character introduced in the crossover story.

cast.name: The visitors
cast.description: The story follows characters from Raiders, PenPals, Xero, AR3NA, Kingdom Kitty, Dillingham, Riggins, and other worlds as they work to return home.
